reason: Start building the gas-exchange surface by combining the thin alveolar lining with its elastic support.
expectation: I expect an elastic structure with alveolar lining, though it may still need airways and blood vessels.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the airways also advances the goal, but I want to build the exchange surface first.

effect: The alveolar sacs provide the exchange surface and elastic recoil; they now need a connection to the airways.
reaction: The link between many small sacs, surface area and recoil is satisfying.
reason: Connect the sacs to the small airways so air can reach them.
expectation: I expect an airway tree ending in alveolar sacs, though the larger airways may still need connecting.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the larger airways is also useful, but I prefer to connect the sacs first.

effect: The alveoli are now connected to fine bronchioles, leaving the larger airways to connect.
reaction: The branching arrangement is clear, though the result adds little explanation.
reason: Connect the respiratory branches to the trachea and bronchi to complete the air passage.
expectation: I expect a continuous airway from the trachea to the alveoli, still needing a blood supply and chest connections.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the chest lining is also necessary, but I want to finish the airway first.

effect: The airways and alveoli now form lungs with a visible slot for the visceral pleura.
reaction: The continuous branching structure is clear, though the covering still needs fitting.
reason: Fit the visceral pleura to the lungs before connecting them to the chest.
expectation: I expect the thin covering to follow each lung's outer surface; the chest lining remains separate.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the chest lining also advances the goal, but I want to finish the lung covering first.

effect: The lungs now have their outer pleural covering and can be connected to the circulation.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward, with no further explanation.
reason: Connect the lungs to the blood supply to build the gas-exchange route.
expectation: I expect lung capillaries to lie close to the alveoli, though breathing still needs the chest and diaphragm.

effect: The circulation now surrounds the alveoli with capillaries, establishing a thin boundary for gas exchange; the chest still needs assembly.
reaction: The distinction between diffusion across walls and a direct opening is useful.
reason: Prepare the chest lining; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the parietal pleura to line the inside of the chest wall, ready for the lungs and diaphragm.

reaction: The cutaway explanation helps distinguish an omitted muscle layer from a hole in the pleural space.

expectation: I expect the diaphragm to fill the lower opening; the lungs and circulation will still need fitting.
